title: Chemical first exits and neighboring coordination loss in energetic perovskites
problem_background: In a family of energetic perovskites sharing the potassium-perchlorate sublattice, changes at the molecular A site can be resolved separately from loss of neighboring local coordination. An atom-resolved comparison of recorded events can determine the ordering of these two processes without interpreting local coordination loss as bulk lattice collapse.

environment.stack_hint: Python standard library for atom-identified event records

approach: For DAP-2, PAP-2 and PAP-H2, analyze three seeds per material at 1666 K using the bundled atom-identified first-exit, A-to-K neighborhood and K–Cl6 persistent-loss records. Verify the A-site heavy-atom join and each fixed eight-K neighborhood. Compute the median of its neighbors' 500 fs persistent loss onsets and compare it with the recorded 500 fs persistent chemical first-exit onset. Preserve right-censoring and aggregate by seed before material; neighboring A sites are not independent replicas.

reproduction_target.summary: Determine whether persistent A-site chemistry generally precedes loss of neighboring local K–Cl coordination and which persistent first-exit operations predominate across the matched materials.
reproduction_target.scope: Analysis-level reproduction from genuine, bundled 1666 K event observations for three A-site variants. Local ordering and reaction-operation distributions are descriptive, not causal or bulk-structure claims; no exact published fraction is requested.

assets.name: Atom-identified 1666 K event observations
assets.description: Three compact CSVs at https://github.com/SchrodingersCattt/pap-h2-research-arm/tree/main/task/data: exits.csv records atom-identified persistent first exits and their operations, neighborhoods.csv maps each A site to eight K units, and k_sites.csv records independently computed K–Cl6 persistent loss onsets. Download these real source records to reproduce the event-level analysis.

workflow.title: Validate atom-identified source events
workflow.action: Check the one-to-one A-site heavy-atom join, nine complete 192-site seeds, eight distinct neighbors per site and explicit 500 fs support-loss onset/censoring fields.

workflow.title: Join chemical and local-support events
workflow.action: Join each recorded chemical first exit to the median 500 fs coordination-loss onset among its eight fixed neighboring K units; retain each site and its support censoring.

workflow.title: Summarize the material-level claim
workflow.action: Compute material- and seed-resolved ordering and first-exit operation distributions from the per-site records and state the supported qualitative pattern.

outputs.description: One row per initial A site with atom-linked first-exit and neighborhood support-loss timing, explicit censoring and operation identity.
Seed-resolved ordering and reaction-operation distributions recomputed from site_events.csv, plus a qualitative interpretation within local-coordination scope.

scoring.summary: Evaluate per-site event coverage and consistency; derive material- and seed-resolved distributions from the site records and assess whether the qualitative interpretation follows.

constraints: Retain all initial A sites, censoring, the 500 fs chemical and geometric persistence criteria, seed identity and 10 fs versus 100 fs sampling distinction. Do not infer the immediate H acceptor from net N–H loss or call local K–Cl loss bulk framework collapse.
